name: Benko Gambit
subtitle: A pawn today. Pressure that lasts.

ideas.idea: Unlike a quick king hunt, the Benko seeks lasting queen-side activity. Let White take a wing pawn, then challenge the pawn that arrives on b5. Open files and a long bishop diagonal can give your pieces clear work even after queens are exchanged.
ideas.structure: White's advanced central pawn gains space but also makes the queen-side structure less flexible. When the a- and b-files open, White's remaining queen-side pawns can become targets. Your own centre needs care: queen-side activity is not a reason to ignore a central breakthrough.
ideas.pieces: The king's bishop usually develops on the long diagonal. Rooks work on the open queen-side files, and knights can support pressure against b2 or help control the centre. Connecting the rooks is often more valuable than rushing a premature invasion.
ideas.motifs: Watch converging pressure on a queen-side pawn, exchanges that remove a key defender, and entry squares along the open files. These are usually positional threats rather than a forced tactical sequence. Do not confuse an attractive diagonal with a bishop that actually has a target.
ideas.declined: If White protects or advances the b-pawn, or declines the first capture, the files may remain closed. Attack the relevant pawn chain and develop normally. An early central pawn push can change the character entirely; meet that challenge before following a memorized queen-side plan.
ideas.caution: White can return material or use the centre to blunt the pressure. The gambit does not guarantee a favorable endgame: if your rooks cannot find targets, the missing pawn still counts.

modelGames.summary: A textbook Benko. Black trades light-squared bishops, puts heavy pieces on the open queenside files and plants a knight on d3. The pressure eventually breaks White's queenside.

moments.title: Open files for the pawn
moments.note: Black is a pawn down, but the a- and b-files are open and the bishop on a6 is about to trade off White's best minor piece.

moments.title: Heavy pieces on the queenside
moments.note: Queen on a6, rooks soon to follow. Black's pieces line up against a2 and b2, the targets the gambit created.

moments.title: A knight on d3
moments.note: The knight lands on d3, deep in White's camp. With White's light-squared bishop gone, nothing can easily chase it away.

moments.title: The c-pawn joins
moments.note: ...c4 supports the d3 knight and adds another lever on the queenside. Black is playing on the side where he has more open lines.

moments.title: A tactical blow
moments.note: Nf2+ forks the king and the e4 pawn. When pieces are active and well placed, tactics appear on their own.

moments.title: The queenside collapses
moments.note: Black's pieces have broken through on the queenside and White's position falls apart. Patient pressure has paid for the gambit pawn many times over.

modelGames.summary: White accepts the pawn, gives up castling, then walks his king to g2. A knight on b5 blunts Black's queenside play. Once queens come off, White's extra material and passed pawns decide.

moments.title: Artificial castling
moments.note: The king walks to g2 behind the g3 pawn. It takes a few tempi, but White now has a safe king and an extra pawn.

moments.title: Block the b-file
moments.note: A knight on b5, backed by a4, blocks the file Black wanted to use. Blunting the open lines is the defender's main task against the Benko.

moments.title: Trading queens
moments.note: White offers the queen trade. Without queens, Black's activity counts for less and the extra pawn counts for more.

moments.title: Winning the exchange
moments.note: The knight takes the rook on a8. White has turned positional pressure into concrete material.

moments.title: A passed b-pawn
moments.note: White's b-pawn is now passed and backed by the rook. Black's pieces must stop it, leaving the kingside defenceless.

moments.title: Promotion is near
moments.note: The pawn reaches b7. The defence held early on, and White's material edge decided the endgame.
